sources.extractedEvidence:
## Tell Claude what it can’t see
Only write down what Claude can’t find by reading the repo, or what it would otherwise spend time rediscovering every session.

## Keep CLAUDE.md short
Claude Code loads `CLAUDE.md` into every session, which means every line in it takes a little of Claude’s attention on every task, whether it’s relevant or not. That’s why the file works best when it only holds what Claude couldn’t work out from the code itself.

## Give Claude a check to run
Give Claude something it can run that comes back pass or fail. Once it has that, it can keep going on its own and you don’t have to watch.

## Keep cost and context down
With a 1M-token window on most current models and compaction near the top of it, you’ll rarely run out of context. You can still pay for context you don’t need, though. Every request sends the whole conversation, so a session that’s collected three unrelated tasks re-reads all three on every turn of the fourth.

## Run sessions in parallel
When you have separate pieces of work going at once, give each its own checkout so the edits can’t collide. `claude -w feature-auth` starts a session in a new worktree, the desktop app runs several of these side by side, and cloud sessions run them in the cloud instead of on your machine.

## What you can stop doing
Every one of these was good advice when it was written. Most were workarounds for something the model couldn’t reliably do yet, and the models have since caught up.
